newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end higher as Reliance leads rally.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end higher as Reliance leads rally.

text.p: Reliance Industries led the charge as share prices on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed higher on Tuesday, spurred by heavy institutional buying, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 12.95 points higher at 726.01.

"Apart from selective buying by domestic financial institutions, short-covering in the highly active shares, mainly Reliance Industries, also aided the recovery," said Summit Gandhi of brokers Rare Financial Services.
Reliance Industries rose 10.80 rupees, or 4.22 percent, to 266.80 rupees.
Brokers said trading was confined only to selected blue chip companies as investors were waiting for the annual budget to be presented before making any new commitments.

"Market has adopted a cautious wait-and-watch strategy at the moment, any major movement in share prices is likely to come only after the government announces the fiscal budget," said another broker who asked not to be named.
Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is expected to present the 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget on February 28.
TISCO surged 7.30 rupees to 187 on heavy buying by domestic financial institutions and speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India quoted 11.15 rupees higher at 269.70.
Larsen and Toubro rose 3.50 rupees to 235.50 on scattered buying support from speculators, brokers said.
